name: What Should Be Included in a Commercial Construction Bid?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a commercial construction bid in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a commercial construction bid in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: A commercial construction bid should be specific enough that the owner can compare offers on the same scope. At minimum, it should define the work included, exclusions, allowances for finishes or fixtures, schedule assumptions, permit responsibility, insurance coverage, payment milestones, and how change orders will be handled. It should also identify whether the contractor is carrying demolition, hauling, temporary protections, inspections, and utility coordination. In Los Angeles County, bids become difficult to compare when one contractor includes items that another leaves out, such as engineering, plan check support, or after-hours work. Owners should ask bidders to clarify all assumptions about site access, existing conditions, and subcontractor pricing. A bid that is clear on scope and exclusions is often more valuable than a lower number with hidden gaps. This is especially important on tenant improvements, office buildouts, and occupied-property work where schedule and coordination matter as much as price.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good bid should clearly define the scope, exclusions, allowances, schedule, permit responsibility, payment milestones, insurance, and change-order process. It should also identify materials, labor, subcontractor work, and any assumptions about site conditions. Vague bids often lead to disputes, delays, and unexpected extra costs.
